title: Full body 3x Week
author: Noah M.
desc: For my father in our garage gym. Good way to get your foot in the door with lifting!

ex.note: Put the bar on the dip bar. Add weight to bar. Get under the bar (on top of your upper traps, right on top of traps). Make sure you have a pad under non-working knee. Drive knees over your toes
Use your hands as hooks. Drive through your elbows. Try to bring your lower sternum to the bar. Do not worry about if your chin goes over. Keep chest up
Try to minimize the mount of lower back used. Pause at the top of the rep, and slowly lower the weight down til you cannot go any lower.
Put your feet on the bench and keep back flat. Go as low as comfortable on your shoulders. You can have a slight bend in the elbows. Drive elbows together. Do not crab the weight.
Either stand or sit with these. Sweep the weight out to around a 45 degree angle. Lean slightly forward. You can have a slight bend in the elbow. Do not have a 90 deg angle with your arms.

Put your upper back on the pole, feet slightly in front of you. You can also do these seated with back support. Keep your arms supinated the entire rep. Do each arm same time or alternate to your pref
Do these on the floor or on the bench. Do not do if elbows hurt. Do a close grip pushup instead. Drive elbows back initially and then try to keep them there.

Load bar on the ground. Deadlift the bar up by grabbing bar, keeping lower back flat, and thinking about pulling up and back. Then lower the bar as close to your shins as possible, going to below knee
Try to lean forward. Go as low as comfortable on your shoulders. Try to come to a 90 deg angle with your forearm and upper arm. Put feet where comfortable (infront, harder, or behind you, easier)
Deadlift dumbbells onto knees. Drive one knee up, launching a DB to a shoulder. Repeat so both DB are in starting position. Have DB either flared out or slightly in front. Do not touch DB tg at top
Have non-working arm and leg supported on the bench. Drive arm up and around the torso. Make sure your upper arm is making anywhere from a 90-45 degree angle with torso. This is for upper back
Hold yourself down onto the bench as hard as you can. Sit up while you do this. Drive up the weight and pause at the top. Slowly lower weight down
Have a neutral grip with your curl. Support your back again. Do these either alternating or the same time. Do not pronate or supinate wrist. Try to not allow upper arm to sway too much
Keep back flat on pad. Grab a grip that is either shoulder width or slightly closer. Try to keep elbows tucked. Flaring uses more chest. Touch lower sternum and then drive up in an arching pattern
Elevate your heels with a plate. Use a pair of dumbbells. Drive knees over the toes. Get as low as comfortable while keeping the lower back flat. Doing a pulsing style of rep
Place bar onto of dip station. Put bar on upper traps. Stick your butt out and back while keeping lower back straight. Feel stretch in hamstrings and then come up, shooting hips through
Try driving elbows to hips. Try to touch lower sternum to the bar. Do not worry about if your chin goes over the bar
Set the incline to around 30 degrees. Do the same kick up method as shoulder press. Try to have elbows flared at 45 degrees. Try to keep back flat.
Do either seated or standing and bent over. Have wrists somewhere from completely pronated to 45 degrees. Sweep dumbbells out. Try to avoid shrugging the weight back. Focus on moving upper arm.
Put the bench on an incline. Grab a Dumbbell and stand behind the bench. Slowly lower the weight down. Try to allow your arm to travel to make close to a 180 deg angle. Have whole upper arm on pad
Set arm back as far as comfortable. Can do these sitting or standing. Do kick backs if this hurts your elbow. Grab top of handle of dumbbell. Drive weight up and slowly lower. Pause at bottom
